method_reconstructed: Fry onion, tomato, ginger and chilli; add the puree.
Fold in paneer cubes and finish with cream.
contested_points: Paneer's antiquity in India is debated — some readings find acid-set cheese early, others argue it arrives much later. Either way, this dish is not old.
Tomato and chilli both post-date the classical texts by centuries.

changed.driver: the dish is modern; what can be restored are its parts, not its ancestry

ingredients: 3/4 cup thick curd, hung 30 minutes — in place of cream
1/3 cup soaked kabuli chana, ground to a paste — in place of cream or cornflour as the thickener
250 g paneer, or the chana paste alone if you want to go further
2 tbsp cold-pressed mustard or sesame oil
steps: Soak the kabuli chana overnight, boil until soft, grind to a smooth paste with a little of its water.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds, shock it cold, puree coarse.
Warm the oil, fry grated ginger and cracked pepper, add the spinach.
Stir the chana paste in and let it thicken for five minutes.
Take it off the flame before folding in the hung curd, or it will split.
The chana gives a body closer to what a period gravy actually was: thickened with a ground pulse, not with dairy fat or cornflour. More protein, more fibre, much less saturated fat.

verification.note: Classed MODERN_DISH. No ancient original is claimed and no locus is cited, so there is no citation to verify. The component restoration is culinary reasoning, offered as such.
